summary: - _(c) Extend or direct Respondent to extend the time for FTC for 90 days so that the Petitioner can inject infirm power and subsequently commission the Project;_ - _(d) Direct Respondent to permit injection of infirm power during the extended period for the purpose of trial run and commissioning;_ - _(f) Pass such other and further order(s), direction(s), and relief(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice._ _During the pendency of the Petition, allow the Petitioner to inject infirm power in respect of the balance 42 MW capacity forming part of the Solar Project._ - (j) The delay in commissioning the balance 42 MW capacity of the Barmer Solar Project is not attributable to the Petitioner and is the direct consequence of multiple unforeseen and unavoidable events beyond the Petitioner’s reasonable control, including inter alia: - (m) Since any extension beyond the said statutory ceiling can be ordered only by this Commission in exercise of its regulatory powers, the Petitioner has been compelled to institute the present Petition, inter alia, seeking extension of time for injection of infirm power along with extension of FTC approval. - (n) In terms of the proviso to Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code, the present Petition ought ordinarily to have been instituted at least fifteen (15) days prior to the expiry of the earlier approved period for injection of infirm power. In this backdrop, the Petitioner seeks relaxation and condonation of the intervening delay. The said delay has occurred for bona fide and procedural reasons. The present Petition was filed on 06.07.2026 after a delay of 6 days; thus, the Petitioner seeks condonation of delay in filing the instant petition under the Commission’s power to relax. _“The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking extension of time for injection of infirm power along with extension of First Time Charging (FTC) approval, for test run and commissioning in respect of the balance 42 MW capacity forming the part of the Petitioner’s Barmer Solar Project. The learned counsel submitted that the Petitioner has already commissioned 196.1 MW out of 250 MW of envisaged Project_ _2. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as under:_ - _(b) The Respondent to file its reply, if any, within two weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder, if any, within two weeks thereafter._ - _(c) The Petitioner to file the following information/clarification, on an affidavit, within two weeks:_ - _(i) The communication of RLDC by which the Petitioner was permitted an extension for injection of infirm power up to 15.7.2026._ # ** Submission of Petitioner in Compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 22.07.2026: ** **4.** The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 07.08.2026 in its submission in compliance with the RoP for the hearing dated 22.07.2026, has mainly submitted as under: - (d) The Petitioner has furnished the copy of commissioning certificates dated 14.03.2026, 27.03.2026 and 26.06.2026. - (f) In view of the corrected position, the present Petition, though earlier described as being confined to the balance "42 MW" capacity, is, in fact and in correct terms, confined and restricted to the balance 38.1 MW capacity forming part of the 221 MW tranche of the Petitioner's Barmer Solar Project, and the reliefs sought in the present Petition, including the interim prayer, ought to be read and understood accordingly, i.e., as being confined to 38.1 MW and not 42 MW. (iv) Pass such other and further order(s), direction(s), and relief(s) as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice. _“At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner is seeking an extension of 90 days for injection of infirm power along with extension of FTC approval, for test run and commissioning in respect of the balance capacity forming the part of the Petitioner’s Barmer Solar Project and the grounds for seeking such extension have been indicated in the affidavit filed by the Petitioner. He further added that the extension ought to be granted from the date of the Commission's final order._ _2. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the matter was reserved for order.”_ **10.** The Petitioner is seeking an extension of time to inject infirm power for a period of 90 days to carry out trial run and commissioning. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that in terms of proviso (b) of Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code, the present Petition should have been filed 15 days prior to expiry of the earlier approved period of infirm injection. The present Petition was, however, filed on 06.07.2026, with a delay of 6 days; therefore, the Petitioner has also sought condonation of the delay in filing the instant petition. **11.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondent and the documents placed on the record. **Issue 1: Whether the delay in filing the instant Petition can be condoned? Whether the Petitioner can be granted an extension of time to inject infirm power for the balance capacity of 38.1 MW?** **18.** The Petitioner has prayed for the condonation of the delay of 6 days in filing the instant Petition. **19.** Considering the submissions of the Petitioner, we condone the delay in filing the instant Petition. Further, we note that the Petitioner is at an advanced stage of commissioning of its project and has already declared COD for 200 MW out of 250 MW solar project. title: Petition under Sections 79(1)(c) and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 19(3) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2024 seeking extension of time for injection of infirm power for the balance capacity and extend or direct NRLDC to extend the time for First Time Charging for the balance capacity; and under Regulation 57 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 read with Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 seeking relaxation/condonation of delay for filing the present Petition. Khaba Renewable Energy Private Limited
